children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to ask you some questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, attending sixth form, college, or an approved training course)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do - I live in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions:

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live somewhere else (for example, at university accommodation or with someone else)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me - he lives with his dad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for that information.

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** (This could include things like clothes, food, pocket money, or contributions towards his accommodation - and would need to be at least the same amount as Child Benefit, which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child or £16.95 per week for additional children)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his clothes, school supplies, and things like that - I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm a few final details:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex** (such as his dad, or anyone else he's living with)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his dad isn't claiming it - nobody else is getting Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Alex's age and education**: Although Alex is 18, he's still in approved education (sixth form studying for A-levels). You can continue to claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

✓ **Your responsibility for Alex**: Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're still considered responsible for him because you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep. You're contributing about £30 per week for his clothes and school supplies, which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child.

✓ **UK residence**: You live in the UK (Leeds).

✓ **No duplicate claims**: Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**What to do next:**
You can make a claim for Child Benefit. If you'd like to proceed, you should contact HMRC or apply online.

**One thing to be aware of:** If you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
